CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the CSV lists 'Karimnagar'; the temple is at Kaleshwaram village in Jayashankar Bhupalpally district (~125 km from Karimnagar, per the South Indian History Congress study), at the Triveni Sangamam - the confluence of the Godavari and Pranahita with the unseen Saraswati (Antarvahini). One of the three Trilinga Kshetrams (with Srisailam and Draksharamam); also called Dakshina Gangotri / Dakshina Triveni Sangamam. Unique feature: two Shiva lingas - Kaleshwara (Yama, granted a place beside Shiva after penance) and Mukteshwara (Shiva, granter of moksha) - on a single pedestal. Legend: a Vaishya's abhisheka with hundreds of milk pots flowed as milk into the sangamam; the Mukteswara linga has two holes (nostrils) into which poured water is said to disappear and join the rivers. Chalukya-built, Kakatiya-renovated; major modern access came after the mid-1970s.

town_description: Kaleshwaram is a village in Jayashankar Bhupalpally district, Telangana, on the banks of the Godavari at the Triveni Sangamam - the confluence of the Godavari and Pranahita rivers (with the unseen Saraswati). Near the meeting point of Telangana, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh. 125 km from Karimnagar, 115 km from Warangal, 60 km from Mancherial, 277 km from Hyderabad (per SIHC study).
